subject.title: Google Chat: Add user OAuth support for reactions and media uploads

question: Should the bundled Google Chat plugin add first-class user OAuth credentials for reactions, native media upload, reaction typing, and proactive DM lookup, or should it remain service-account-only with narrower fallbacks?
rationale: The issue adds new credential/config surface and security-sensitive OAuth routing, so maintainer intent is needed before automation can choose the permanent product shape.

options.title: Approve plugin-owned user OAuth
options.body: Implement user OAuth inside the Google Chat plugin with SecretRef/redaction support, scoped auth clients, tests, docs, and clear fallback behavior when OAuth is absent.

options.title: Limit work to fallback mitigations
options.body: Land or refine media-link fallback work separately and keep reactions, native uploads, reaction typing, and proactive email-alias DMs unsupported for now.

options.title: Defer bundled OAuth
options.body: Keep the bundled Google Chat plugin service-account-only until a maintainer-sponsored design or external plugin proves the broader OAuth model is worth adopting.

recommendation.title: Approve plugin-owned user OAuth
recommendation.body: Implement user OAuth inside the Google Chat plugin with SecretRef/redaction support, scoped auth clients, tests, docs, and clear fallback behavior when OAuth is absent.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue as a maintainer-side routing decision and is tied to foundational Google Chat commits.
